by: a closure attribution session, from judging/DEP.settled.json (each cell's why, why2 and ev) and REQUIREMENTS.md's DEP rows. Rules follow the axes the judges name: R for the shape's handover and kernel, S for group commit (DEP-12), V and N for a third voter (DEP-15), N for pooled processes (DEP-04, DEP-18), L and H for packing (DEP-20), Q and R for OBJ's PUT cost (DEP-21), R lww where v4's own merge breaks (DEP-02, DEP-05). Eight V4 overrides follow v4 as built: its own timed runs (DEP-01, DEP-03, DEP-04, DEP-13), its door (DEP-10 S), its unbatched fsync (DEP-12, as in PERF-DATA), its directory with no project id (DEP-18), and its own dir needing no migration (DEP-19)

rules.basis: BUY: rolling the NATS servers moves each stream's leader. E-44 timed only an unplanned kill (5.2 to 7.2 s to a new leader on JetStream's own timer); a planned step-down and a roll were not run

No row ran J's four-roll test. The parts are measured on etcd, not on fero: a handover pauses the group 9.7 to 9.8 ms at the median, and A-02 adds 'refuse at once, never drop' (E-13). Three copies in about 1 s is a sum of measured parts with no real machine restart, and the other shapes' handovers (a writer epoch, a seal, a lease, an in-sync set) were not run at all

V4.basis: v4 as built ran J's test: four rolls of three durable members, no failed call, no lost or doubled write, 3.6 to 5.0 s each against 10 s, longest client pause 108 ms (STATUS.md; REQUIREMENTS DEP-01). The pass is a run of v4's own code, not an option: no axis tag says a row was built and timed, so a row that only shares some of v4's tags must not borrow it

parts.why: Only V4 differs, and it passes on a run of its own build (override). Every other row is open because no roll ran on it; the judges name the handover each shape would roll with (Raft's transfer, a writer epoch, a seal, a lease, an in-sync set, the outside log), so R decides the open cells.

rules.basis: V4 (referee): v4 reports no caught-up number and opens its write gate by membership, not by the rows it holds (api/index.ts); STATUS.md records a member back inside the eviction window that says writable about 100 ms before it holds its peers' rows, which is this requirement's own test. The other rows' judges tie the fault to the replication: with one writer per group a restarted copy cannot take a write on its own, but under R lww any member takes writes. V4 takes no fix (AMENDMENTS 3)

With one writer per group a restarted copy cannot take a write on its own, so v4's fault cannot come back in the same form. parts.why: V4 fails on its own run; the judges of the other 19 rows say one writer per group keeps that fault from coming back, so R decides.

rules.basis: BUY: after all three NATS servers restart, each stream elects on JetStream's own timer, which fero cannot set: E-44 measured 5.2 to 7.2 s to a new leader after a kill. That points over 2 s, but a restart-all was not run

SLOG and RLOG: the log tier or log members stay up while the servers restart, so the writer only reloads and takes its log again (SLOG: a seal and re-take; RLOG: reasoned from A-14's rules). Neither path was modelled or run as a restart-all

OBJ: no election; the first server back takes the lease by a conditional PUT (1.37 ms p50 on MinIO, E-28) and loads the manifest. A restart-all was not run, and how long it waits for the old lease is not stated

After every copy restarts no group has a leader. A member that waits its election timer (2 to 2.5 s in TS by A-02) is writable too late for the 2 s bar; E-26 measured three cold TS Raft processes writable in 20 groups after 265 to 318 ms only when the first one campaigns at once. No row states who campaigns at boot, and no restart-all with rows ran

A native row's election timer is under 1 s with A-02's jitter, so the first leader stands inside about 1.25 s plus the boot (reasoned from E-13's failover times). It leaves room on paper, but no restart-all with rows ran on any native kernel

rules.basis: V4 (referee): a v4 member whose fold is empty at boot applies its data: seed, and tombstones are collected within a heartbeat, so a fresh joiner's seed row looks new and last-writer-wins spreads it: a deleted row came back in 2 runs of 2 on v4 63e0679 (STATUS.md), this requirement's own regression case. The spreading is the R lww merge; the skip-seed-on-join fix is not in the row and V4 takes no fix (AMENDMENTS 3)
BUY: on JetStream the seed is a publish by whichever process creates the stream, so two creators both seed unless the publish carries an expected-sequence check. E-44 ran no seed

A seed applies at create and the catalog keeps a 'seed applied' mark (DESIGN-V5 4.2, 6.1), so a joining copy folds the log and never seeds. But the mark and the seed rows sit in two places, and nothing ran a crash between the two or two creators at once (E-33's seeds are founding members, not data: seeds)

rules.basis: BUY (referee): JetStream is the base the row was built and priced on (E-44, E-41); its persisted mode is sync_interval: always, which fsyncs each message alone: 3,668 a second from one publisher and 3,275 from 16 clients (E-09b), against PERF-09's 50,000. fero cannot change the store
PD: S lsm was not run in this study. A write group shares one WAL sync in RocksDB and TiKV's raft engine (cited from memory); no pipeline of this shape was measured here

OBJ: a commit is one PUT for every write in a commit window, group commit by design with a PUT in place of an fsync (E-41 assumes 10 ms). E-28 timed single 1 KB PUTs only (1.37 ms p50 on MinIO); no batched pipeline ran
OBJ: a commit is a PUT (R obj), so group commit is many writes per PUT; no batched pipeline ran (E-28)
OBJ: a commit is a PUT (Q put), so group commit is many writes per PUT; no batched pipeline ran (E-28)

E-02's pipeline, in TS, Rust and Go, writes every queued record with one writev and one fdatasync on a journal per process: 2.8 million 100 B appends a second in TS, against v4's 250; one shared journal keeps 740 to 890 fdatasyncs a second for 16 to 2,000 groups (E-12), the form E-11 runs under the Raft ports

ISR: a log file per group still commits each group's queue with one fdatasync: 1.39 to 2.25 M appends a second in Node at 16 to 256 groups (E-12, mode b), far over PERF-09's 50,000. Its tail is PERF-08's matter

SLOG (referee): E-02's followers are log nodes in shape: each appends the writer's batch to its journal, runs one fdatasync per batch and acks, 2.8 million appends a second in TS; even a file per loglet shares each fsync and reaches 0.59 to 2.25 million (E-12), against 50,000

rules.basis: BUY (referee): its log runs on three NATS servers of the project's own; every JetStream replica is a full copy, so there is no log-only voter and no platform tier that stands in as the third, and a project cannot run on two copies (E-41, E-44)

ISR: the in-sync set (Q isr) shrinks to the survivor; not run or modelled

OBJ: the object store holds every commit, so either copy's crash takes no vote away, and the other takes the lease by a conditional PUT (1.37 ms p50, E-28). The lease takeover by CAS on the manifest was never modelled, and no crash test ran

The row has no log-only voter and no log tier (V +lrn or full; N proc or pool): two copies are two voters, so a crash of either stops writes, and F-11's third voter must be a third full copy (E-41 prices three machines). rules.basis: Closure referee B (judging/closure/hybrids/B.settled.json): a TypeScript phase that keeps its log and rows in an LSM still ships the LSM as a native addon (the study names no LSM written in TypeScript), so the TS rows' "no native part" does not hold; no fero tarball with one was packed.

The row ships plain TypeScript and data, and that shape passed the test: a 192-line build strips types and copies data inside the package, and example 02 ran on Node 22 and 26 from a 451 KB tarball of v4 (STATUS.md, 'fero on npm'). The server or daemon is a native binary beside Node (SRV a Rust or Go server, PD a Rust server and controller, EMB-V8 a Rust binary with V8 inside, SIDE a daemon per host). rules.basis: OBJ: a commit is one PUT (Q put). At 10 writes a second, 100 ms apart, every write is its own commit: 26.3 million PUTs a month, $131 at $0.005 per 1,000, so $135.80 against $10 with the subscribers inside (E-41, E-28). 13.6 times the bar, the same under AMENDMENTS 1.3's restated bar; fewer PUTs would need a commit that waits over 2 s
OBJ: in R obj a commit is a PUT (SPACE 2), so 10 writes a second cost about 26.3 million PUTs a month, $135.80 against $10 (E-41, E-28), as worded and restated

else.basis: AMENDMENTS 1.3: the $10 bar does not place the 100 subscribers. With them inside, E-41 puts the rows at $4.94 to $18.21 at 10 writes a second (SRV $11.64, BUY $15.90, PD $18.21: over, but under two times, on prices read from search summaries and assumed machine counts), and every row under $2.19 asleep. Open as worded and restated

parts.why: Only OBJ differs, and its judges name the PUT commit (Q put; R obj defines a commit as a PUT). The other rows' figures differ in size but every judge holds them open on the same two grounds: the bar's unplaced subscribers and prices from search summaries.
